page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.16-256 is an Arm-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. It features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz on the arm64 architecture. With one thread per physical core, the instance uses dedicated CPU allocation rather than simultaneous multithreading, ensuring predictable execution without thread-level resource competition.

The hardware configuration pairs these 32 cores with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. There is no bundled local storage integrated with this instance type, meaning persistent storage must be attached over the network. Hardware graphics accelerators are not included, as the GPU count is zero. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned alongside the instance.

With its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, this instance is structured for workloads that demand significant memory capacity per compute unit without requiring local disk storage. The predictable per-core performance delivered by the Ampere architecture makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, large caching layers, distributed data processing, and containerized microservice deployments optimized for arm64.

Due to its dedicated core architecture and substantial memory capacity, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory data stores, distributed caching layers, data processing frameworks, and arm64 container environments.
